title: Bristol And NQCC Launch Intensive Quantum Computing Courses
excerpt: Bristol and NQCC offer intensive six-week online Quantum Computing Courses taught by leading experts, designed for STEM students & professionals.
content:
The National Quantum Computing Centre (NQCC) and the University of Bristol are launching intensive online courses designed to rapidly upskill a specialized workforce. Aimed at students, researchers, and industry practitioners, the NQCC is further supporting participation by offering bursaries to those in the growing quantum sector, recognizing the need for advanced skills in areas like quantum algorithm development and computing architectures. These courses form part of the NQCC’s support in enhancing skills and learning in quantum computing in the UK.

Intensive Courses Enhance UK Quantum Skills

Each course spans six weeks, incorporating two break weeks within that timeframe, designed to accommodate the schedules of working professionals and researchers seeking to deepen their expertise in quantum computation. Specifically, successful applicants will demonstrate pre-existing knowledge of linear algebra, a mathematical tool for understanding quantum systems and algorithms. The NQCC is extending financial support through bursaries for research students and industry practitioners actively engaged within the UK’s quantum start-up ecosystem, recognizing the need to cultivate a skilled workforce driving commercial innovation.

This targeted funding aims to lower the barrier to entry for those already contributing to the burgeoning quantum industry, enabling them to refine their skills and accelerate development. According to the course information, participants can expect a weekly time commitment of approximately 10 hours, balancing recorded lectures with live group sessions and personalized assignment feedback.

These courses, “Introduction to Quantum Information Science and Technologies,” are structured to provide both foundational knowledge and specialized training, with the latter building directly upon the concepts introduced in the former. The first course, running from May 11th to July 10th, 2026, focuses on the core mathematical techniques essential for research in quantum information science and technologies, while the second, scheduled from October 12th to December 11th, 2026, examines key quantum algorithms, the quantum Fourier transform, and quantum error correction. The NQCC’s involvement reflects its broader mission to bolster the UK’s quantum capabilities, acting as a central hub for collaboration between academia and industry, and providing access to a range of quantum computing platforms.

The NQCC, established in 2020 at the Harwell Science and Innovation Campus, operates as a private entity with partnerships including IBM Quantum, Digital Catapult, and Google Quantum AI, and is a key component of the UK National Quantum Technologies program. This collaborative approach extends beyond course development, as evidenced by the Digital Catapult’s ongoing collaboration with the NQCC on the Quantum Technology Access Programme, and the NQCC’s SparQ Access program, which opened 15 quantum platforms to researchers in June.

The recent delivery of the UK’s first 100-qubit quantum computer, built by Infleqtion and received by the NQCC in May, underscores the facility’s commitment to providing resources for both research and skills development. The course descriptions highlight the skills sought after in roles such as developing quantum algorithms, quantum applications, and quantum computing architectures.

This focus aligns with the £2 billion investment in UK quantum computing announced earlier in 2026, signaling a national commitment to establishing the UK as a leader in the field. Registration for the Quantum Computation course closes on September 19th, 2026, while registration for the Introduction to Quantum Information Science and Technologies course closes on April 19th, providing a limited window for interested professionals to secure a place and contribute to the growing UK quantum ecosystem.
